dedupe_keys.name: risevatnet dam cyber intrusion bremanger norway april 2025 waterworld lessons

description: This article analyses the 7 April 2025 intrusion at the Risevatnet dam in Bremanger, Norway, where unknown attackers logged into the remote-control panel, forced a discharge valve fully open for roughly four hours and posted a three-minute screen recording on Telegram under the name of a pro-Russian group. It reports no structural damage or downstream flooding, that the spill triggered Norway's first investigation under Penal Code section 130 on foreign influence operations, and that investigators think a weak password gave access. The author, writing for water utilities, argues that traditional network security misses actions at the physical process layer, Level Zero of the Purdue model, and recommends independent out-of-band monitoring of actual valve and pump states, noting that cybersecurity for water systems is largely optional. Coverage: one dam incident, with sector-wide discussion. Access: a free trade-press article; the licence is not stated. Caveats: the piece comes from a security vendor perspective and the investigation findings are second-hand. It supports cyber-physical resilience and emergency response scenarios for dams, and relates to the ASDSO dam emergency warning lessons record in the catalogue.
